answer: An agent market requires every bidding identity to lock a fixed collateral bond for 30 days before its bids count, and caps each identity’s total unsettled exposure at that bond’s value. Agents trading lotus seeds, haven bookings, or plume illustrations face the same rule. An attacker creating 1,000 identities must lock 1,000 bonds; splitting one budget among aliases buys no extra exposure, while tying up capital imposes financing costs.
